item.title: Asia-Pacific Stocks Poised to Rise as US Markets Rebound
item.description: Regional bourses in the Asia-Pacific were positioned to advance on Thursday morning. The anticipated upward movement followed an overnight turnaround on Wall Street from its session lows.

item.title: Crude Maintains Two-Day Advance Amid Middle East Conflict
item.description: Crude oil preserved its two-day price advance on November 26 as regional tensions persisted. Ongoing hostilities across the Middle East presented risks to the recovery of local petroleum shipments.

item.title: Oracle and CoreWeave Rebound Following Wednesday Morning Slump
item.description: Technology shares including Oracle and CoreWeave recovered from early-session deficits on Wednesday. The broader market selloff diminished in intensity as trading approached the final bell.

item.title: Nvidia Erases Bulk of Monday Rally as Dip Buyers Take Profits
item.description: Shares of Nvidia relinquished a large portion of Monday's advance following profit-taking by dip buyers. Research firm Vanda Research noted that retail investors who purchased shares on the dip last week have seen their gains largely disappear.

item.title: Asian Stocks Point Higher Following Wall Street's Late Recovery
item.description: Equities across Asia were slated for modest advances after a late-session turnaround on Wall Street prevented the Nasdaq 100 from entering a bear market. Meanwhile, persistent uncertainty regarding artificial intelligence investments provided support to US Treasuries.

item.title: SpaceX Secures FCC Clearance for 1 Million Orbital Data Satellites
item.description: The Federal Communications Commission granted SpaceX authorization to place 1 million orbital data center satellites in space. The initiative had faced objections during the regulatory process from Amazon alongside other entities.

item.title: PCE Inflation Gauge Reaches 3.8% in October
item.description: The personal consumption expenditures price index met expectations for an annual inflation rate of 3.8% in October. This reading aligns with the Dow Jones consensus forecast.

item.title: U.S. Proposes New Tariffs on 14 Trading Partners
item.description: The United States government has proposed new levies targeting 14 different trading partners. These measures are intended to address trade practices viewed as discriminatory or burdensome.

item.title: Rising Inflation Expectations Point to Fed Rate Hike
item.description: The Federal Reserve's preferred inflation measure accelerated in October. This trend suggests the central bank will likely increase borrowing costs in the coming month.

item.title: U.S. Proposes New Tariffs Following Court Ruling
item.description: The U.S. government is pursuing new trade levies against China and other nations. This action follows a Supreme Court decision earlier this year that invalidated previous, broader tariff measures.

item.title: Nvidia Faces Regulatory Risks Following CEO Return
item.description: Nvidia shares declined as investors weighed the legal and regulatory implications of Jensen Huang's return. The company now faces heightened scrutiny within the broader artificial intelligence sector.

item.title: Tech Stocks Decline as Markets Await PCE Data
item.description: U.S. equity futures are lower as investors question the outlook for the artificial intelligence sector. Meanwhile, Treasuries have rallied in anticipation of the upcoming PCE inflation report.

item.title: European Gas Markets Face Volatile Winter Outlook
item.description: Low supply buffers and geopolitical instability in the Middle East are expected to drive volatility in European gas markets. Shifting weather forecasts further complicate the supply outlook.

item.title: Taiwan Stocks Fall 8% as AI Enthusiasm Wanes
item.description: Taiwanese stocks dropped 8% as investor optimism regarding Jensen Huang's career prospects faded. Market participants shifted their focus toward broader concerns regarding the global AI trade.

item.title: Huawei Convicted in U.S. Criminal Trial
item.description: A U.S. jury has found Huawei guilty of charges including bank fraud and money laundering. The company was also convicted of conspiracy to commit trade secret theft.

item.title: Houthi Attack on Saudi PIF Tower Results in Injuries
item.description: A strike by the Iran-backed Houthi group on the Saudi Arabian sovereign wealth fund tower left 11 people injured. This incident marks the second attack on the facility within a six-day period.

item.title: India Market Faces Valuation and Tariff Challenges
item.description: Indian markets are contending with high stock valuations and risks associated with global tariffs. Additionally, a liquidity shortage in the banking sector is increasing borrowing costs for lenders.

item.title: Dell Shares Increase Following AI-Driven Sales Growth
item.description: Dell stock rose as the company reported that artificial intelligence demand helped sales more than double. The firm maintains a vetting process for its order backlog to ensure customer quality.

item.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Resigns Amid Allegations
item.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has stepped down from his position. The resignation follows reports of multiple affairs, including one involving an alleged Chinese intelligence operative.

item.title: Data Center Construction Drives Demand for Foreign Steel
item.description: A surge in data center construction is straining domestic steel supplies and increasing prices. Consequently, buyers are increasingly turning to cheaper Asian imports despite existing tariffs.

item.title: Market Decline Deepens Amid AI Skepticism
item.description: Stock markets extended losses as investors grew doubtful about the sustainability of the artificial intelligence boom. Technology shares retreated while Treasury bonds gained due to increased demand for safe-haven assets.

item.title: U.S. Panel Reports Shift in China's Strategy Toward India
item.description: A U.S. panel suggests China is shifting its approach to limit India's economic growth. The strategy appears to favor economic containment over military engagement.

item.title: Australian Bonds Rally on Expectations of Rate Cuts
item.description: Australian bonds are experiencing their longest rally in over five months. Investors are increasing bets on an interest-rate cut by the Reserve Bank due to signs of economic weakness.

item.title: Keppel to Merge Telecom Units M1 and Starhub
item.description: Keppel Ltd. has reached an agreement to combine M1 Ltd. and Starhub Ltd. The merger follows several months of negotiations between the two Singaporean telecommunications firms.

item.title: Oil Prices Decline Amid Optimism Over Conflict Resolution
item.description: Oil prices continued to fall following a significant decline in the previous session. Market sentiment is influenced by hopes regarding efforts to resolve the conflict between the U.S. and Iran.

item.title: Nvidia Shares Rise Amid Investor and Regulator Scrutiny
item.description: Jensen Huang has returned to his leadership role at Nvidia. Market participants and lawmakers are expressing increased caution regarding the company.

item.title: Nvidia Stock Gains Momentum Following CEO Return
item.description: Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia has provided a boost to the artificial intelligence sector. Investors are being advised to anticipate potential price fluctuations.

item.title: U.S. Markets Rally as Jensen Huang Returns to Nvidia
item.description: U.S. stocks experienced their strongest daily performance in over a year on Monday. The market rebound is attributed to renewed confidence in the AI sector following Jensen Huang's return.

item.title: Tech Sector Gains Following Jensen Huang's Nvidia Return
item.description: The broader technology sector saw significant gains after Jensen Huang returned to Nvidia. This development has provided relief to the previously struggling AI market.

item.title: Trump Highlights Importance of Jensen Huang to Nvidia
item.description: President Trump emphasized the value of Jensen Huang's leadership to Nvidia during discussions about corporate governance. He suggested that losing such talent poses a greater risk than current regulatory concerns.
